name: Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination
description: Neural system, neuron structure, nerve impulse, synapse, and parts of the human brain

cards.definition: The process by which two or more organs interact and complement each other's functions
More muscle activity → more O₂ needed → faster breathing, heartbeat and blood flow
Neural: quick, point-to-point connections. Endocrine: chemical integration through hormones.

cards.term: Specialised cells of the neural system?
cards.definition: Neurons: detect, receive and transmit stimuli
A network of neurons (very simple)
A brain with a number of ganglia and neural tissues

cards.term: Two parts of the human neural system?
cards.definition: CNS (brain, spinal cord) and PNS (all nerves associated with the CNS)
Site of information processing and control
Afferent: tissues/organs → CNS. Efferent: CNS → tissues/organs.
"SAME": Sensory = Afferent, Motor = Efferent
Somatic (CNS → skeletal muscles) and autonomic (CNS → involuntary organs, smooth muscles)

cards.term: Two divisions of the autonomic neural system?
cards.definition: Sympathetic and parasympathetic

cards.term: What is the visceral nervous system?
cards.definition: The part of the PNS (nerves, fibres, ganglia, plexuses) carrying impulses between the CNS and the viscera, both ways

cards.term: Sympathetic vs parasympathetic in one line? (intuition)
cards.definition: Sympathetic = "fight or flight" (heart speeds up). Parasympathetic = "rest and digest" (heart slows).
Parts: CNS: brain, spinal cord · PNS: cranial and spinal nerves; Role: CNS: processing, control · PNS: carries impulses to and from CNS

cards.term: Three major parts of a neuron?
cards.definition: Cell body, dendrites, axon

cards.term: What are Nissl's granules, and where are they found?
cards.definition: Granular bodies in the cell body and dendrites (not in the axon)

cards.term: Dendrites vs axon: direction of impulse?
cards.definition: Dendrites: towards the cell body. Axon: away from the cell body.
Bulb-like end of each axon branch, with synaptic vesicles containing neurotransmitters

cards.term: Correction: NCERT's Figure 18.1 labels "Schwan cell". Correct spelling?
cards.definition: Schwann cell (after Theodor Schwann)
Multipolar: One axon, two or more dendrites · cerebral cortex; Bipolar: One axon, one dendrite · retina; Unipolar: Cell body with one axon only · embryonic stage

advancedHtml.backHtml:
Neuron types

Structure · where?

MultipolarOne axon, two or more dendrites · cerebral cortex
BipolarOne axon, one dendrite · retina
UnipolarCell body with one axon only · embryonic stage

cards.term: Beyond NCERT: where are pseudo-unipolar neurons found in adults?
cards.definition: Sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia: one process that splits into two branches

cards.term: What forms the myelin sheath in the PNS?
cards.definition: Schwann cells
Gaps between two adjacent myelin sheaths
In spinal and cranial nerves
In the autonomous and somatic neural systems; the Schwann cell encloses the axon without forming myelin
Myelinated: impulse jumps from node to node (saltatory), much faster. Unmyelinated: slower, continuous along the membrane.
Their membranes are polarised

cards.term: At rest, the axonal membrane is more permeable to?
cards.definition: K⁺; nearly impermeable to Na⁺ and to negatively charged proteins

cards.term: Ion distribution across a resting axon?
cards.definition: Inside: high K⁺ and negative proteins, low Na⁺. Outside: high Na⁺, low K⁺.

cards.term: What does the sodium-potassium pump do?
cards.definition: Actively moves 3 Na⁺ out for every 2 K⁺ in
Outer surface positive, inner surface negative: polarised
The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane (about −70 mV)

cards.term: What happens when a stimulus is applied at site A?
cards.definition: Membrane becomes freely permeable to Na⁺ → rapid Na⁺ influx → polarity reversed (inside +, outside −): depolarised
The potential difference across the membrane at the depolarised site: the nerve impulse

cards.term: How is the impulse conducted from A to B?
cards.definition: Current flows on the inner surface from A to B and on the outer surface from B to A, depolarising B; this repeats along the axon

cards.term: How is the resting potential restored?
cards.definition: Na⁺ permeability quickly falls and K⁺ permeability rises; K⁺ diffuses out: repolarisation

cards.term: Role of Na⁺ in the action potential?
cards.definition: Rapid influx of Na⁺ reverses polarity and generates the action potential
Membrane state: Resting: polarised · Action: depolarised; Outside charge: Resting: + · Action: −; Key ion: Resting: K⁺ leak, Na⁺–K⁺ pump · Action: Na⁺ influx

cards.definition: A junction formed by membranes of a pre-synaptic and a post-synaptic neuron, which may or may not be separated by a synaptic cleft
Electrical: membranes very close, current flows directly, faster, rare. Chemical: fluid-filled cleft, uses neurotransmitters.
Electrical

cards.term: Steps of transmission at a chemical synapse?
cards.definition: Impulse at axon terminal → vesicles move and fuse with membrane → neurotransmitter released into cleft → binds receptors on post-synaptic membrane → ion channels open → new potential

cards.term: The new potential in the post-synaptic neuron can be?
cards.definition: Excitatory or inhibitory

cards.term: Why is conduction across a chemical synapse one-way? (intuition)
cards.definition: Only the pre-synaptic side has neurotransmitter vesicles; only the post-synaptic side has receptors
Voluntary movement, balance, vital involuntary organs, thermoregulation, hunger, thirst, circadian rhythms, endocrine glands, behaviour; vision, hearing, speech, memory, emotions, thought

cards.text: Cranial meninges from outside in: {{c1::dura mater}} → {{c2::arachnoid}} → {{c3::pia mater}}.

cards.definition: "DAP": Dura (tough, outer), Arachnoid (middle), Pia (thin, touches brain)

cards.term: Three major parts of the brain?
cards.definition: Forebrain, midbrain, hindbrain

cards.term: Figure 18.4 · Sagittal section of the human brain

cards.definition: Cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus

cards.term: Most developed part of the human brain?
cards.definition: Cerebrum

cards.term: What connects the two cerebral hemispheres?
cards.definition: The corpus callosum (a tract of nerve fibres)

cards.term: Why is the cerebral cortex called grey matter?
cards.definition: Neuron cell bodies are concentrated there

cards.term: Why is the inner cerebrum called white matter?
cards.definition: Its fibre tracts are covered with myelin sheath (opaque white)

cards.term: Three kinds of areas in the cerebral cortex?
cards.definition: Motor, sensory and association areas
Intersensory associations, memory, communication
Folds pack a larger surface area (more neurons) into the skull
Major coordinating centre for sensory and motor signalling

cards.term: Where is the hypothalamus, and what does it control?
cards.definition: At the base of the thalamus; controls body temperature, eating and drinking; neurosecretory cells secrete hypothalamic hormones

cards.term: Which part acts as the master clock?
cards.definition: The hypothalamus (its suprachiasmatic nucleus sets circadian rhythms)
Inner parts of the cerebral hemispheres and deep structures such as the amygdala and hippocampus

cards.term: Functions of the limbic system (with hypothalamus)?
cards.definition: Sexual behaviour, emotional reactions (excitement, pleasure, rage, fear), motivation; also olfaction and autonomic responses
Thalamus: relays sensory and motor signals. Hypothalamus: temperature, hunger, thirst, hormones.
Between the thalamus/hypothalamus and the pons
The cerebral aqueduct
Four round swellings on the dorsal midbrain
Receives and integrates visual, tactile and auditory inputs
Pons, cerebellum, medulla oblongata
Fibre tracts that interconnect different brain regions

cards.term: Why is the cerebellum surface highly convoluted?
cards.definition: To provide space for many more neurons
Integrates information from the semicircular canals and auditory system: balance and coordination
Cerebrum: forebrain; thought, memory, voluntary action. Cerebellum: hindbrain; balance, coordination.
Control of respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, gastric secretions
Midbrain, pons, medulla oblongata: connects brain and spinal cord

cards.term: Which part of the brain does it?
cards.definition: Temperature, hunger, thirst: Hypothalamus; Balance, posture: Cerebellum; Breathing, heart reflexes: Medulla; Memory, intelligence: Cerebrum; Links the hemispheres: Corpus callosum; Emotions: Limbic system
